newsitem.title: USA: Orphan Medical gets approval, won't market product.
newsitem.headline: Orphan Medical gets approval, won't market product.

text.p: Orphan Medical Inc said Wednesday its Repliderm wound dressing has been granted marketing approval by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) but the company has decided not to market the product.
The company said the FDA approval does not distinguish its product from other wound dressings, which Orphan Medical said is important to successfully market Repliderm.
Therefore, Orphan Medical will not market Repliderm until clinical trials to evaluate its use are completed.
"We are taking this as a step further to show that our product improves the rate of wound healing," a company spokeswoman said.

The FDA approval addresses the use of Repliderm as a collagen-based dressing for the management of skin ulcers, first and second degree burns, post-surgical incisions, cuts, abrasions and other skin conditions.
Orphan Medical said its planned trials will evaluate whether Repliderm accelerates healing of bed sores or pressure ulcers.
Orphan Medical acquires, develops and markets products for well-defined patient populations treated by health care specialists.
